title: Minimum Array Sum
summary: Given an integer array nums and three integers k, op1, and op2, you can perform the following operations on nums: - Operation 1: Choose an index i and divide nums[i] by 2, rounding up to the nearest whole number.
statement: Given an integer array nums and three integers k, op1, and op2, you can perform the following operations on nums: - Operation 1: Choose an index i and divide nums[i] by 2, rounding up to the nearest whole number. You can perform this operation at most op1 times, and not more than once per index. - Operation 2: Choose an index i and subtract k from nums[i], but only if nums[i] is greater than or equal to k. You can perform this operation at most op2 times, and not more than once per index. Both operations can be applied to the same index, but at most once each. The goal is to minimize the sum of all elements in nums by applying any number of these operations.
constraints: nums has 1–100 nonnegative integers; k is positive; 0 <= op1, op2 <= len(nums).
Operation one replaces an element by ceil(value/2), at most once per index and op1 times total.
Operation two subtracts k from a value at least k, at most once per index and op2 times total; both operations may affect one index in either order.
hints: Each element has a small set of legal outcomes consuming zero or one of each operation.
Use dynamic programming keyed by how many operations of each type have been spent.
For every value, enumerate no operation, either operation, and both valid orders; relax the next budget table.
Every legal global plan chooses one local outcome per index, and the two budget counts contain all cross-index dependence.
editorial: Every legal global plan chooses one local outcome per index, and the two budget counts contain all cross-index dependence.

tests.explanation: Halve 19 to ten and subtract three from eight, reducing the original sum 35 to 23.
Halving first gives five, then subtracting five reaches zero.
